answer: Each oracle identity locks an 80-credit bond on the quartz ledger. Each epoch it signs one task count. A prism rule sorts reports into a spectrum and takes the median; reports over 10% away burn the bond. An echo of the median is published, and any oracle may challenge it. A new oracle pays 10 plus 5 per earlier oracle, so the kth fake costs 80 plus 5k+5, the 1000th 5,085, and 1,000 fakes 80,000 locked plus 2,507,500 in fees, with no report reusable. A copy-report ring fails: a copied report carries another key and burns every copier bond. An honest oracle locks 80 once and pays 10 once.
